examples.label: Scan the common web-app ports across the whole scope list

notes: Feed the results into EyeWitness/Aquatone rather than clicking each host - vhosts on the same IP look identical by port alone. Add the scope's vhosts to /etc/hosts first or name-based apps won't resolve.

recommended.note: Screenshot every live web app the scan found.
Alternative screenshotting/report tool from the same nmap XML.

name: Application Discovery - Nmap Web Ports
description: Scans a scope list for the common web/application ports (including alternate HTTP ports like 8080/8180/8500) and saves all output formats. The XML feeds screenshotting tools like EyeWitness/Aquatone.

defense.why_it_works: Web-facing services expose version banners and default paths. Nmap service probes retrieve HTTP Server headers and SSL certificates, reliably fingerprinting CMS platforms, app servers, and middleware without authentication.
defense.prerequisites: The target ports must be reachable; no credentials required. Banner grabbing works against any unfiltered TCP service.
defense.impact: Attacker maps the full application footprint — web servers, CMS versions, management interfaces — enabling precise CVE selection before attempting exploitation.
defense.detection: Log Nmap's TCP SYN + service-probe traffic (rapid sequential connections from one source IP across many ports). IDS signatures for Nmap version-scan probes (Snort SID 1-469). Host-based: correlate rapid new connections in netflow.
defense.artifacts: IDS/IPS alerts for port scan patterns | Web server access logs showing version-probe GET requests | Firewall connection logs (high connection rate from single IP)
defense.prevention: Run all management interfaces on non-standard ports behind a VPN or ACL. Suppress version banners: set ServerTokens Prod (Apache), server_tokens off (nginx). Use a WAF that blocks scanner fingerprints.
defense.misconfiguration: Default Nmap scan hits open port 8080/8443 with verbose banners (e.g., Apache Tomcat/9.0.30) and exposed /manager, /admin, /console paths because no server-token suppression or network ACL exists.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Apache default
ServerTokens Full
ServerSignature On
# Tomcat server.xml default
<Connector port="8080" Server="Apache-Coyote/1.1"/>
defense.secure_config:
# Apache
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
# Nginx
server_tokens off;
# Tomcat server.xml
<Connector port="8080" Server=" "/>
# Network: restrict /manager, /admin to internal IPs only
defense.evasion: Slow-rate scan (--scan-delay 5s, -T1). Fragment packets (-f). Use --randomize-hosts. Decoy scanning (-D RND:10).
